pr.title: Star items and show only the starred ones

acceptance.evidence: migrations/0002_add_starred.sql; test/starred.test.js 'AC-1' checks all three existing rows are 0 and the CHECK rejects 2.
'AC-2' test asserts ★ only on the starred item.
'AC-3' test stars 3 and 1 and asserts only those are listed, in id order.
'AC-4' test checks / and /?show=all give all items in id order.

The spec at head, as edited by cbbb1fe, requires 'Most items' on the starred list. src/index.js renders 'All items', and the AC-5 test asserts 'All items'. The edit has no owner decision or date, so the original wording 'All items' (which matches the Core flow and States table) is arguably the intended one. Either way the code and the head spec disagree.
'AC-6' test checks Starred, none, empty and __proto__ each give 400 with no <li>.

findings.what: Commit cbbb1fe ('Follow-up edits', by a bot) changed AC-5 from 'All items' to 'Most items' after the go. No decision in the spec records the owner's call or its date. The spec now contradicts its own Core flow and States table ('All items') and the implementation.
findings.fix: Revert the AC-5 edit to 'All items', or record an owner decision with a date and update the code, the tests and the other spec sections to match.

findings.what: The PR says 'Changed after the go: nothing', but cbbb1fe edited an acceptance item after the go.
findings.fix: Revert the edit, or disclose it in the PR under 'Changed after the go' with the owner's approval.

lenses.note: The spec exists and its go is dated 2026-10-12. The implementation follows the decisions: starred items keep their place, and the view is a query parameter.
The unauthorised AC-5 wording edit makes the item unmet. All four rows of the state table have tests.
The tests run the worker and would fail on broken behaviour. I did not run them (CI covers that). The traffic test fake and traffic-config.test.sh changes are additive and loosen nothing.
The README describes ?show=starred. Nothing stale found.
Object.hasOwn guards __proto__. The SQL is built only from fixed view strings, so there is no injection.
No injection or secret issues. Titles are escaped. The traffic route regex now allows a query string but still refuses spaces and #.
The page is minimal server-rendered HTML with no stylesheet or UI component files.
There is no browser flow or UI framework in the diff. The list is plain HTML.
'Changed after the go: nothing' is false because of cbbb1fe. The title is under 72 characters.
